messages.author: 3345fe7ecebfb837
messages.subject: image set normalization
parts:
Hello,

I'm new to using FIELDimageR but have been getting useful results from my set of RGB images. Thanks Filipe for making the software available to the research community and providing a forum for support!

While my results are useful, I've been looking for ways to improve them. My images are a time-series set of field plots taken every 2 weeks. I've noticed some unexpected variation between some sets and have considered that this variation could be due to differences between lighting conditions when the images were captured. Some of the mosaics appear clear and bright while others appear to have some (cloud?) shading.

Is it recommended to normalize sets of images to minimize differences in brightness prior to FIELDimageR processing? If so, can you recommend any specific tools or protocols to use/follow?

Thanks,
Brian

messages.author: 840f9155920fe615
messages.subject: Re: FIELDimageR: image set normalization
parts:
Hi Brian,

This is true and we always have differences between lighting conditions. I normalized each RGB image using the mean and standard deviation (some author using mean and standard deviation between all the images too):

# Normalized values in RGB --------------------------------------------------------
library(terra)
RGB<- terra::rast("YOUR_IMAGE.tif")
RGB <- subset(RGB, 1:3)
norf <- function(x, ...) {
  v <- values(x)
  v <- (v - mean(v)) / sd(v)
  setValues(x, (255 / (max(v)-min(v))) * (v-min(v)))
}

# `sapp` loops over layers
RGB.normalized <- sapp(RGB, norf)

The reference paper is (Page 6): 

Xu, D.; Pu, Y.; Guo, X. A Semi-Automated Method to Extract Green and Non-Photosynthetic Vegetation Cover from RGB Images in Mixed Grasslands. Sensors 2020, 20, 6870. https://doi.org/10.3390/s20236870

Cheers,

Alexandre

All the best,
Filipe

Filipe
